cases.why: an escaped backtick ends the template early, so the rest of the template is lexed as code and a `//` in its text is cut as a comment. The real template has no escaped backtick today, so the build stays green and only this case would notice.
a `/` inside [...] ends the regex, so /[/'"]/ is cut short and its quote opens a string that swallows the code after it. The real template has no such class today; the build stays green.

a block comment that held a line break is replaced by a space, so `return a /* ...\n... */ b` becomes `return a b`: automatic semicolon insertion no longer ends the return after `a`, and the code means something else without any syntax error.
